I've farmed these 7 mu for a long time. Let me think through this year like I always do — start from what I did last year and adjust a little.

My main land is wheat-maize rotation. I keep about 5 mu in that rotation because that's my best flat ground near the well. I put 1 mu in cotton on the sandier corner where wheat doesn't do as well. The remaining 1 mu I split — half mungbean, half red bean. Beans don't need much and I use them for the house and to sell a bit at market.

For wheat this year, I'll sow Jimai improved variety again — my neighbor Old Wang got good yield with it last season. I use one bag of compound fertilizer (about 40 kg NPK 15-15-15) per mu as base, then top-dress with urea (about 15 kg) at jointing. That gives roughly 16 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. I water 3 times — before winter, at jointing, at grain filling. The well makes this easy. Pesticide twice — once for aphids, once for rust if I see it.

For maize after wheat, I plant hybrid seed (Zhengdan or similar). Maize eats more nitrogen than wheat, so I use more urea — maybe 18 kg N total, with base compound and one top-dress at big trumpet stage. Water 2 times if rain is short. One spray for corn borer.

Cotton needs more care — I use more fertilizer and spray more times because bollworm and aphids are bad. Hybrid Bt seed. About 15 kg N, heavier on P and K.

Beans I don't fertilize much — they fix their own nitrogen. Just a little compound at planting, one watering, one spray if aphids come.

I plough before wheat every year — rotary for maize after wheat because there's no time. Cotton I plough deep.
